AddDoc.description:
[`BOARD_DOCS`]' body: the Doc to link, a [`Pointer::Doc`] or a
[`Pointer::MachineDoc`] (a machine's agent links its own machine's), to
the board's strip, or with `row` (`row_…`) to that row.

AddMany.description:
[`BOARD_ENTRIES_MANY`]' body: exactly one of `pointers` (those items) or
`untriaged` (everything that matches, but the `except` pointers). More
than [`ADD_MANY_MAX`] is refused, 400: narrow the filter.

added.description: Rows made. An item on the board already isn't counted.

attached.description: PRs attached to the row of the issue they close, as a single add does.

AnswerAsk.description:
[`BOARD_ASK_ANSWER`]'s body: one of the ask's `option`s, or `text` when
it has none.

AnsweredAsk.description: An ask that was answered, kept in the row's history.

Ask.description:
A question on a row that a person answers on the board (Arugula #367):
asked by a person or an agent, or raised by the board itself from the
state of the row's items (`raised`, never stored, and with no answer).

asked_by.description:
Who asked, as a name: a person, or an agent and its machine. Empty
for a raised ask.

can_answer.description: The reader may answer it: the person it names, or an owner or editor.

mine.description: It is for the reader (a raised ask is for whoever reads the row).

raised.description:
The board raised it, from its items' state, and it clears with its
cause: nobody answers it.

who.description: The account it is for; empty for a raised ask.

who_name.description: Who it is for, as the reader's page names them.

AttachBlock.description:
[`AGENT_PROJECT_ATTACH_BLOCK`]'s body: the issue as the starter wrote it
(`#N`, `owner/repo#N` or `IDENT-N`) and the block, which is on the
signing machine.

session.description:
The starting session's name (Arugula #765): it holds the issue's row
from now (with `take`, moved from whoever held it, who is told).
Absent for a caller with no name: no hold is made.

take.description:
Take a row that another machine's block holds, folding that block
under `earlier`; without it the attach is refused, 409 `claimed`.

oneOf.description: The work itself: a PR, an agent block or a run. It moves the lane.
Evidence that the work is done: a run or a link.

take.description:
For an agent block as work on a row another machine's block holds:
take the row over. The old block is folded under `earlier`.

block.description: A `Block` pointer's block as its machine last reported it.

live.description:
The item's state now, when the reader may see it: an item they can't
read says nothing, as an unreadable row does.

released.description:
A block that a newer agent took the row from (`take`): it is an
earlier agent whatever it reports, and holds no claim.

BlockAttached.description:
[`AGENT_PROJECT_ATTACH_BLOCK`]'s answer: the rows the block is on now
(also those it was on already), and none when no board of the project
has a row for the issue.

BlockOn.description: One row a block was attached to.

BlockState.description:
What a daemon says of one of its own agent blocks, and all it says
(aru-116's second ruling): the state word, the branch, the short HEAD,
whether it is pushed, how many files are uncommitted and the diffstat.
No message text, no file names, no prompts: the type has no field that
could carry them. This is the view, read leniently by a daemon; control
refuses a body with another field through [`BlockStateReport`].

title.description:
The name its starter or its person gave the block: a board's chip
for it. Never the first words of a prompt.

BlockStateReport.description:
[`BlockState`] as a daemon reports it (aru-116's second ruling): the same
fields, but a body with another one is refused, so no message text, file
name or prompt can ride along. It is only ever parsed by control, from a
daemon; [`BlockState`] is what everyone reads.

BlockWord.description: What an agent block is doing (aru-116's second ruling).

closed_at.description: When it was closed; absent while it is open.

closed_by.description:
The account that closed it; empty once that account is deleted. When
an agent closed it, the account it acted for.

closed_by_agent.description: The machine whose agent closed it, if one did.

created_by.description:
The account that made it; empty once that account is deleted. When an
agent made it, the account it acted for.

created_by_agent.description: The machine whose agent made it, if one did.

done_note.description:
What was done, written when the board was closed; kept when it is
opened again. Empty before it was ever closed.

goal.description: What the board is for, in a paragraph; empty means none.

lead.description:
The session that leads the board (#414): a post on the board's thread
reaches it. Absent when no session does.

progress.description: How many of its issues are closed.

source.description:
The tracker's epic it follows, when it was made from one (Plane's,
#483); absent for a board a person made.

BoardDoc.description: One Doc of a board: in its strip, or on one row (a row's [`Row::docs`]).

added_by.description: The account that linked it (the owner, for an agent).

agent.description: The machine whose agent linked it, if one did.

copy.description:
A machine Doc's copy on the platform (`pdc_…`), when it sits in this
board's project (native #673): the title and counts are then the
copy's, and the chip opens it while the machine is away. Older
platforms don't send it.

machine_name.description: A machine Doc's machine, by name.

missing.description: A project Doc that was deleted.

BoardLead.description:
The session that leads a board: the machine it runs on and its name there,
as that machine's daemon matches it (#414).

at.description: When the session took the lead.

machine_name.description: The machine's name now; empty while it can't be told.

BoardProgress.description:
A board's work, counted: the rows with a primary item (an issue or a
PR; a note row is never counted). `done` is those in the Done lane, and
`proven` those of them with a proof; `review` and `doing` are those in
the Review and Doing lanes.

BoardReachProject.description: A project a machine's board grants reach, as its owner reads it now.

BoardSettings.description: What a project says about its boards (Arugula #404).

stall_minutes.description:
A Doing row whose blocks have all been idle for longer than this many
minutes (1 to [`STALL_MINUTES_MAX`]) is stalled.

BoardSource.description:
The epic a board follows: its children are the board's rows, and the
connection made the board, not a person.

connection.description: The connection that made the board, as the project calls it.

key.description: The epic's key in the tracker, such as `ARUGU-10`.

left_out.description:
How many children the board is too full to show, the oldest done
ones first.

started.description:
Whether the epic is started in the tracker (Plane's `started` group),
read from its mirrored item; not whether the board is open.

url.description: Where the epic is in the tracker's web app.

BoardView.description:
A board with its four lanes, in order (`lane_next`, `lane_doing`,
`lane_review`, `lane_done`), each with its rows, and its groups, in
order. The rows of a group are those with [`Row::group`] set to its id; a
row without one comes after the grouped ones.

chain.description:
The longest chain of open rows (`row_…`), first to last; empty when
no row waits on another (#762).

docs.description:
The Docs strip, in order. Empty for a board with none; an old client
ignores it.

groups.description: Empty for a board with none; an old client ignores it.

order.description:
Every row (`row_…`) as the board stores them: by group, in the
groups' order, then by position inside each, those with no group
last. A move that names the order it read (`seen`) names a group's
rows from here.

ready.description:
The ready set (Arugula #403): the rows (`row_…`) with an issue or a
PR as their item that are in Next and have no open blocker.

said.description:
What a write did that the board alone doesn't say: a PR attached to
the row of the issue it closes, an item that was there already.

sequence.description:
The rows (`row_…`) that have a [`Row::step`], by step, and inside a
step by what unblocks the most open rows, then by position (#762).

Category.description:
Where an item is in its own life, the same words for every source
(Arugula #405): Plane's state groups, which a native issue's and a GitHub
issue's open and closed map onto. A lane reads it: `completed` and
`canceled` are Done, every other category is not.

ChatAgent.description:
The agent that wrote a message (M197): the machine whose grant it acted
through, and its name now. The message's author is the machine's owner.

session.description:
The session that posted, as its machine called it then (#429): an
agent block's title, or the Claude Code session's name. Display
only; never what a permission rests on.

CheckClaim.description:
[`AGENT_PROJECT_CLAIM_CHECK`]'s body: the issue as the starter wrote it
and the asking machine (the signer).

session.description:
The asking session's name (Arugula #765): another session's hold on
the row, on this machine or another, is a claim; its own is not.

ClaimChecked.description:
[`AGENT_PROJECT_CLAIM_CHECK`]'s answer: `held` says who holds the row
(the sentence of the 409 at attach), none when nothing does.

CloseBoard.description: `POST` to close a board: what was done, not empty.

Diffstat.description: A `git diff --stat` summary line as numbers: nothing of the files.

DiffstatReport.description: [`Diffstat`] as a daemon reports it: a field it doesn't list is refused.

DocBoards.description:
[`PROJECT_DOC_BOARDS`]' answer: the project's boards that list the Doc,
open ones first.

DocOnBoard.description: A board that lists a project Doc.

rows.description: How many rows carry it as a reference.

EditBoard.description: `PATCH`: what to change; a field left out stays. An empty goal clears it.

EntryKind.description: Zone (a group, in a database; a lane, on the wire) or row.

oneOf.description: A group; `group` is read as this too.

Group.description:
A named, ordered section of a board that its author sets: a phase, a
wave, an area. A row belongs to at most one ([`Row::group`]); a group
holds no lane, and a row's lane is the same in any group.

progress.description: Its rows with an issue or a PR, counted as a board's are.

HoldRow.description:
[`BOARD_ROW_HOLD`]'s body: what is left, 1 to [`HOLD_MAX`] characters
once trimmed, on one line.

Lane.description:
Where a row is, worked out on every read from the live state of its
items and never stored (aru-125). Each is the furthest that applies, in
the order `done`, `review`, `doing`, `next`.

oneOf.description: Nothing is under way, or the row is a note.
An agent block that isn't closed, or a run that is running.

A PR is open, or the issue is open and its PR merged (see
[`Mark::NotFinished`]).
The issue is closed, or the PR merged or closed.

LaneSet.description: A lane a person set on a row ([`Row::lane_set`]).

by.description: The account that moved the row.

LaneView.description:
One of a board's four lanes as a read answers it, with its rows. The wire
and TypeScript still call it a zone (`zones`, `BoardZone`).

LeadBoard.description:
`POST` to [`AGENT_BOARD_LEAD`]: the calling session takes the board's
lead (`session`, its name on its machine), or with `release` the lead is
cleared, by the machine of the session that leads or by a person.

LeftQueue.description: A PR's last unmerged exit from its merge queue (Arugula #766).

at.description: When the platform heard it, in milliseconds.

reason.description:
GitHub's `reason` as it came, in upper case: `CHECKS_TIMED_OUT`,
`CHECKS_FAILED`, `MERGE_CONFLICT`, `MANUAL`, `BRANCH_PROTECTIONS`,
`GIT_TREE_INVALID`, `INVALID_MERGE_COMMIT`, `UNKNOWN_REMOVAL_REASON`.
One GitHub adds later is kept as it is.

oneOf.description: Not done; `why` says.

LinkResult.description: One link's outcome, in the order it was given.

LinksDone.description:
[`AGENT_PROJECT_RELATIONS_BATCH`]'s answer: one result for each link of
`add` and of `remove`, in order.

Live.description:
The item a row points at, as it is now: what the page draws beside the
row's own status, and the label of its link.

assignees.description:
Who an issue or PR is assigned to: a mirrored item's logins, a native
issue's names. A run has none.

category.description: An issue's status category; a PR and a run have none.

closed_by.description:
With `closed_with`, the words of the PR that closed it: `"(#12)" in
the title`, `"Closes #12" in the body`, `the branch feat/12-x`,
`attached to its board row as work`. Absent for a close from before
they were kept.

closed_with.description:
A closed native issue that a merged PR closed: the PR
(`OWNER/NAME#N`), so a wrong close is easy to spot (Arugula #743).

identifier.description: A tracker item's project key (`ARUGU`: the card reads `ARUGU-12`).

kind.description:
`pr` or `issue` (a mirrored one), `native` for a native issue, or
`run`.

labels.description:
The item's labels (#547): a native issue's, a mirrored item's, a
Plane item's. A run has none.

left_queue.description: A PR that left the queue unmerged, and why (`ForgeItem::left_queue`).

provider.description: `plane` for a tracker's item; absent for GitHub, native issues and runs.

queued.description:
A PR in its branch's merge queue now (Arugula #766). A repo with no
queue, a platform from before it and every other kind say false.

queued_since.description: With `queued`: when it entered the queue, in milliseconds.

repo.description: `OWNER/NAME` of a mirrored item; absent for a native issue.

state_name.description: A tracker item's own state (`In Progress`).

title.description: A run's: how it started (`manual run`).

url.description: Where a tracker item is, in the tracker.

LiveState.description:
What a pointer to an item, an issue or a run is now, from data control
already has (the forge mirror, the issues and runs tables): a separate fact, never written
over the row's stored `status`.

oneOf.description: A PR or an issue, open.
A PR, open, with checks still running.
A PR, open, with red checks.
A PR closed unmerged, or an issue closed.
A run, running.
A run that failed.
A run that is pending, approved, denied, canceled or expired.

Mark.description:
A note on a row that its lane doesn't say, worked out on every read and
never stored (aru-125, decisions 7 to 9).

oneOf.description:
What a build before Arugula #841 said of an open issue whose PR
merged, with none open: read as `NotFinished` with no reason and
`merged`. Current platforms never send it.

The row's issue is marked Not finished (Arugula #841), or it is open
and a PR of the row merged, with none open: a merge doesn't close a
marked ticket. `merged`: a PR of the row merged, and the row is in
Review. `reason` is what is left, and is none when nobody marked it
(a merged PR that only said `part of`). A marked row with nothing
merged keeps the lane its work gives it.

by.description:
Who marked it: a login or name, and for an agent "<person>'s
agent on <machine>" as the board names an agent.

oneOf.description:
The row's item was canceled (a Plane `cancelled` state, a native issue
closed as not planned or as a duplicate): the row is Done and never
proven, whatever merged.

An open PR of the row is stacked on another open PR: it targets that
PR's branch, so it waits for it. `repo` is left out when the reader
may not read the repo.

An agent block attached to the row (`attachment`) was closed, and
another may have taken its place: it no longer counts toward Doing.

The row is in Doing, every block of it that isn't closed has been
idle for longer than the project's `stall_minutes`, and no PR is on
it (Arugula #404). `since` is when the last of them went idle, in
milliseconds. It names no block: who holds the row is the block's
chip, for a reader who may see it.

The row's item is blocked by an open item (a `blocks` edge, Arugula
#403): the row stays in its lane. `number`, `title` and `repo` are
left out when the reader may not read the blocker (one such mark
stands for all of them: "something you can't see").

board.description:
The other board the blocker is a row of, when the reader may read
the blocker and it is on a board other than this one.

lead.description: The session that leads that board, when one does.

oneOf.description:
The row's item is in a loop of open ordering edges (Plane can make
one): it shares its `step` with the others in the loop.

MoveDoc.description:
[`BOARD_DOC_MOVE`]'s body: the Doc it goes before, in the same strip or
row; none: last.

MoveEntry.description:
[`BOARD_ENTRY_MOVE`]'s body. A row moves to a group (`zone`) or, with
`zone: null`, out of its group; with `zone` absent it stays where it is.
It goes before `before` (a row of the place it goes to), last without
one. A group moves among groups:
`before` is a group, `zone` is absent. A lane is never set (aru-125): a
`zone` that is a lane is refused.

`seen` is the row ids of the group the row goes to, in the order the
caller read them. A row's `rev` doesn't count moves, so this is what a
move that mustn't overwrite someone else's checks: if the group's rows
aren't those, in that order, nothing moves and the answer is 409
`stale_order` with the group's rows as they are now ([`StaleOrder`]).
Absent, a move is made whatever the order.

zone.description:
The group the row goes to; `null`: none. Absent: its own. `group`
is read as this too.

NewAsk.description:
[`BOARD_ROW_ASK`]'s body: `who` is an account of the project. `options`
are 0 to [`ASK_OPTIONS_MAX`] (none: free text), and `recommend` is one
of them.

goal.description: What the board is for; left out: none.

lead_session.description:
With an agent's write: the session that makes it leads the new board
(#414). A person's write ignores it.

NewRelation.description:
[`PROJECT_RELATIONS`]' body: `from` `kind` `to`, each end an `iss_` or
`fi_` id of the project (`a` blocks `b`: from a, to b).

Pointer.description:
What a row points at. `None` is free text. The ids are the platform's:
`fi_…` (a mirrored PR or issue), `iss_…`, `run_…`, `hw_…`, `pdc_…` (a
project Doc).

oneOf.description: An agent block on a machine.

pane.description: The block's pane, as `%N` or `N`; stored as `N`.

oneOf.description:
An `https://` URL, as evidence (a CI page, a report). The platform
takes only `https`, no userinfo, at most [`LINK_MAX`] bytes.

A project Doc (`pdc_…`) of the board's own project. Only a Doc strip
or a `reference` attachment carries one.

A Doc block on a machine. `title` is a snapshot from when it was
linked, since the machine may be off; a [`BoardDoc`] reads the
machine's copy instead when the copy sits in the board's project.

Proof.description:
The mark on a Done row that is proven. A Done row without one is not
proven yet.

pointer.description: What proves it: the merged PR, or the evidence attached.

ProofBy.description: How a Done row is proven.

oneOf.description:
A PR of the row merged with every check on its head completed and
none red.
A `proof` attachment.

PutBlockState.description:
[`AGENT_BLOCK_STATE`]'s body: the pane (of the machine that signs it) and
its state.

age_ms.description:
How long ago, in milliseconds, the machine saw the block in this
state: more than none when the report waited out a failure to reach
control. A machine that sends it (0 included) also sends each live
block's state again every [`BLOCK_STATE_EVERY_MS`], so control counts
one of its reports older than [`BLOCK_STATE_STALE_MS`] as unknown.
None: a daemon from before Arugula #745, whose report is as of now
and never goes stale.

PutEntry.description:
[`BOARD_ENTRIES`]' body. Without `id` it adds a row, last (`entry` is
`row` or absent), or, with `entry: zone`, a group with a `title`, last;
with `id` it changes that row or group: what is absent is left as it is,
and a change to `pointer`, `note` or a group's `title` names `rev`. A
new row's `zone` is the group it goes in. `kind`, and a `zone` that is a
lane, are refused, and so is every `status` (aru-125: lanes follow the work;
a question for a person is an ask, #367). The row's
`pointer` is an issue or a PR (or a link, for a note).

kind.description: Refused: a group has no kind.

status.description: Refused: ask with a question instead.

zone.description: A new row's group (`zon_…`); `group` is read as this too.

Relation.description: An edge made, as [`PROJECT_RELATIONS`] answers it.

RelationDirection.description: Which end of an edge a row's item is.

oneOf.description: The row's item is the first end: it blocks, duplicates, was found from.
The row's item is the second end: it is blocked by the other.

RelationKind.description:
What an edge between two work items says (Arugula #403). Only `blocks`
gates: it keeps the blocked item's row out of the ready set until the
blocker is closed. `before` (#761) says an order and gates nothing; it
can't close a cycle with `blocks` edges.

oneOf.description: The first item blocks the second.
The first item duplicates the second.
The first item was found while working on the second.

The first item comes before the second, in the order the work is
done in.

RelationSource.description:
Who made an edge. `plane` and `github` edges are read from there, and
Arugula doesn't change them.

ReleaseSessionHold.description:
[`AGENT_BOARD_ROW_SESSION_HOLD_RELEASE`]'s body: the calling session, by
its name. Only the holding session may let go: another's is refused.

Resolution.description:
One reference, resolved: the `pointer` it names, or `why` it names none
(nothing by that number, or several linked repos have it and the project
has no native issue of it: the answer names them).

item.description: The reference as it was written.

ResolveItems.description:
[`AGENT_BOARD_RESOLVE`]'s body: up to [`RESOLVE_MAX`] references, each
`#N`, `owner/repo#N`, `IDENT-N` or an `iss_`/`fi_` id.

Resolved.description: [`AGENT_BOARD_RESOLVE`]'s answer, one for each reference, in order.

agent.description:
The machine whose agent added the row, if one did (it may remove
it; nobody else's agent may).

ask.description: The row's one open question: asked, else raised by the board.

asked.description: The last [`ASKED_SHOWN`] asks answered, newest first.

attachments.description: Work and proof attached to the row, oldest first.

block.description:
A `Block` pointer's block as its machine last reported it, when that
machine holds `boards.write` over the board's project.

docs.description:
The Docs linked to the row (#517): its spike or research, in order.
They move no lane and prove nothing.

group.description: The group (`zon_…`) the row belongs to, if any.

held.description:
The session that holds the row's issue (Arugula #765), if one does.
Never set on a row whose issue is closed.

lane.description: Where the row is, from the live state of its items.

lane_set.description:
Set when a person moved the row and the work hasn't changed its
derived lane since (#494): `lane` is then the row's lane.

live.description:
A `fi_`, `iss_` or `run_` pointer's state now, when the reader may see the
item ([`BoardView`] is read with it; a write's answer has it too).

marks.description:
What the lane doesn't say, in a fixed order: `not_finished`,
`cancelled`, `after`, `blocked_by`, then one `earlier` for each closed block.

place.description:
The column the row sits in on the Steps chart (Arugula #824): the
same longest-path layout as [`Row::step`], but over every row with an
issue or a PR, done ones included, using their ordering edges whether
the other end is open or closed. So finishing work never moves a row.
Absent for a row with no issue or PR.

proof.description: Set only on a Done row that is proven.

relations.description: The edges of the row's item, both ways, for the drawer.

sessions.description:
The agent sessions started on the row's issue, oldest first
(Arugula #843). A live one puts the row in Doing.

status.description:
Kept for old clients: `needs_input` when the row has an open ask
(#367), `none` otherwise. Nothing writes it.

step.description:
Where the row falls in the board's order (Arugula #762): 1 plus the
highest step of the open rows that come before it, worked out on
every read and never stored. Absent for a row with no issue or PR,
and for a Done row. Doing and Review rows are step 1.

RowCandidate.description: One thing a row may point at.

assignees.description: GitHub logins for a mirrored item; account ids for a native issue.

labels.description:
The item's label names: a native issue's, a mirrored GitHub or Plane
item's. A run has none.

pointer.description: What a row takes as its pointer: `Issue`, `ForgeItem` or `Run`.

repo.description: `OWNER/NAME` of a mirrored item; a tracker project's name.

state.description: `open`, `closed` or `merged` for an issue or a PR; a run's own state.

title.description: A run's: how it started (`manual run`).

url.description: Where a tracker item is, in the tracker.

RowRelation.description: An edge of a row's item, as the reader sees it.

item.description: The `iss_` or `fi_` id of the item at the other end, with `other`.

other.description:
The item at the other end. Left out when the reader may not read it:
the edge is "something you can't see", with no title or number.

removable.description: The reader may take it off: an owner or editor, and it was made here.

RowSession.description: An agent session started on a row's issue (Arugula #843).

branch.description: The one ref it may push, `arugula/<8 hex>-<slug>`.

live.description:
Whether it moves the row: it is under way, or done with its PR not
yet sent. A session that isn't live is shown dimmed.

pr.description: Its PR's link, once its asker sent it.

state.description:
Its state as the platform keeps it: `queued`, `working`,
`needs_input`, `done`, `failed`, `unresponsive` or `stopped`.

SessionHold.description:
The session that holds an issue's row (Arugula #765): the one that last
started an agent on it, or took it. It is the issue's, so a row on two
boards shows the same holder, and it lasts until the issue closes or the
session lets it go. The same shape as [`BoardLead`].

at.description: When the session took the row.

machine_name.description: The machine's name now; empty while it can't be told.

session.description: The session's name, as its machine's daemon matches it.

SetLane.description:
[`BOARD_ROW_LANE`]'s body. `reason` goes with `done` on a native issue:
`completed` (when not given), `not_planned` or `duplicate`.

StaleOrder.description:
The body of a move refused as `stale_order`: the group's rows now, in
order.

Status.description: Where a row stands. `None` says nothing.

UntriagedQuery.description:
Which untriaged items [`AddMany`] adds: a [`WorkQuery`] with `untriaged`
set, of the board's own project.

WorkItems.description: [`PROJECT_WORK`]'s answer: the newest first, across sources.

labels.description:
With `untriaged`: the labels of everything that matches `q`, `label`
aside (so the chips keep their counts), most items first, then by name.

next.description: With `untriaged`: the cursor of the next page, null at the end.

total.description: With `untriaged`: how many items match `q` and `label` in all.

WorkLabel.description: A label and how many of a query's matches carry it.

cursor.description:
With `untriaged`: the page after the one that answered this
[`WorkItems::next`]. Opaque; it holds its place when items leave the
list between pages.

label.description: With `untriaged`: only items with this label.

limit.description: At most this many (default 30, at most 100).

order.description:
With `untriaged`, `new` (the default) or `old`: by when an item was
last updated.

q.description:
Search words: an issue's title or body, a mirrored item's title or
mirrored content, a run's trigger (`manual`).

untriaged.description:
Only open issues (native and GitHub) that no row of any of the
project's boards points at.

ZoneKind.description:
A zone's kind: every zone a read answers is a `lane`, one of the four
([`Lane`]). No one makes a zone.
